reasons.claim: The chain runs Isma'il, his brother, Sulayman, Sharik, then Anas, one link each, as both readers have it.
reasons.quote: قال حدثني أخي، عن سليمان، عن شريك بن عبد الله بن أبي نمر، سمعت أنس بن مالك

reasons.claim: Anas is the last link; what follows is his account, not a further transmitter.
reasons.quote: سمعت أنس بن مالك، يحدثنا عن ليلة

reasons.claim: The report is related from al-Zuhri with no named route before him, so he is the first written link.
reasons.quote: رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلزُّهْرِيِّ

reasons.claim: Ali b. al-Husayn speaks to al-Zuhri in the narrated encounter, so he is the last link (ruling 9).
reasons.quote: قَالَ لِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ

reasons.claim: Five taḥwīl branches, the first with two co-transmitters, all close on Isma'il, which the text writes once.
reasons.quote: كلهم عن  إسماعيل، بهذا الإسناد

reasons.claim: The last branch is Muhammad b. Rafi' from Abu Usama.
reasons.quote: ح وحدثني محمد بن رافع، حدثنا أبو أسامة

reasons.claim: The mention of Ibrahim b. Humayd's version is a wording remark, not a route.
reasons.quote: نحو حديث إبراهيم بن حميد

reasons.claim: «عمي» introduces Abd Allah b. Wahb, one link.
reasons.quote: حدثنا عمي عبد الله بن وهب

reasons.claim: Abu Yunus is a link and «مولى أبي هريرة» only describes him; the chain ends at the second Abu Hurayra.
reasons.quote: أن أبا يونس، مولى أبي هريرة حدثه عن أبي هريرة

reviews.question: al-Faqih's statement of the compiler's routes («طرق») to a source, with no saying

reasons.claim: The first route runs from the compiler's father through Sa'd, Ahmad, al-Husayn b. Sa'id to Fadala.
reasons.quote: فقد رويته عن أبي- رحمه اللّه- عن سعد بن عبد اللّه

reasons.claim: A second route opens with its own first link and is written in full, so it is a separate group.
reasons.quote: و رويته عن محمّد بن الحسن

reasons.claim: The opening mention of Fadala names the source of the book, not a link; if the owner rules these route statements are chains, this structure is right, and if not, no chain is stored.
reasons.quote: و ما كان فيه عن فضالة بن أيّوب

reasons.claim: Ibn Abi Umayr relays Ibn Udhayna.
reasons.quote: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ قَالَ قَالَ اِبْنُ أُذَيْنَةَ

reasons.claim: Zurara is only addressed and is not a link (ruling 4).
reasons.quote: قُلْتُ لِزُرَارَةَ

reasons.claim: Muhammad b. Muslim and Bukayr are co-transmitters from Abu Ja'far, the last link.
reasons.quote: يَرْوِيَانِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ

reasons.claim: al-Nufayli and Sa'id b. Mansur are co-transmitters from Abd al-Aziz.
reasons.quote: حدثنا النفيلي، وسعيد بن منصور، قالا

reasons.claim: Salim answers in Salih's presence and relays from his father, from Umar.
reasons.quote: فسأل سالما عنه فقال سمعت أبي يحدث عن عمر بن الخطاب

reviews.uncertainty_note: Maslama asks the question; ruling 3 could make him a link, but Salih heard Salim directly, so he is better read as only present.

reasons.claim: The second branch has two co-transmitters from Hisham, then a tail shared by both branches up to Sa'd.
reasons.quote: حدثنا هشام بن عمار، حدثنا حاتم بن إسماعيل، وإسماعيل بن عياش، عن يحيى بن سعيد

reviews.question: al-Faqih's statement of the compiler's routes («طرق») to a source, with no saying

reasons.claim: The route runs from the compiler's father through al-Himyari, Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa and al-Bazanti to Abu Jamila.
reasons.quote: فقد رويته عن أبي- رضي اللّه عنه- عن الحميريّ

reasons.claim: If the owner rules these route statements are chains, this structure is right, and if not, no chain is stored.
reasons.quote: و ما كان فيه عن أبي جميلة

reasons.claim: Two isnads follow the saying: the first ends at Samura, and the second has Shu'ba and Sufyan as co-transmitters ending at al-Mughira.
reasons.quote: عن شعبة وسفيان عن حبيب

reasons.claim: «قالا» refers to the two Companions, and the Prophet is the end of the chain, not a link.
reasons.quote: قالا قال رسول الله
